scope: Public-source breadth review against 117 existing professions. No private profiles, outcome-driven target counts, live catalog edits, or salary assumptions.
method: Official BLS OOH duties and entry requirements, current O*NET occupation details and code checks. These are proposed editorial interest questions; no claim of psychometric validation.

sources.title: BLS: Health Education Specialists
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s entry; assess community needs, develop health teaching and evaluate programs; some employers require or prefer certification.

sources.title: BLS: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists and Technicians
sources.keyEvidence: Specialists typically need bachelor’s; inspect work environments and investigate incidents; professional certification is employer-dependent and may require experience. Technician is a different entry route.

sources.title: BLS: Genetic Counselors
sources.keyEvidence: Master’s genetic counseling with supervised clinical rotations; most states license; accreditation, exam and certification matter. Interpret inherited risks and support informed decisions.

sources.title: BLS: Athletic Trainers
sources.keyEvidence: Master’s from accredited program; nearly all states require licensure or certification. Clinical injury prevention, evaluation and rehabilitation differs from fitness coaching.

sources.title: BLS: Microbiologists
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s entry; some employers prefer graduate degrees. Research microorganisms and carry out laboratory experiments.

sources.title: BLS: Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s entry; master’s for higher-level work, PhD to lead research. Study wildlife and ecosystems in field/lab settings.

sources.title: BLS: Agricultural and Food Scientists
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s typical entry; some roles require graduate degrees. Plant/soil science licensing can depend on state and duties; internships recommended.

sources.title: O*NET: Animal Scientists
sources.keyEvidence: 19-1011.00: research genetics, nutrition, reproduction, growth and development of domestic farm animals.

sources.title: O*NET: Soil and Plant Scientists
sources.keyEvidence: 19-1013.00: crop/plant growth, pests and soils; research alternative practices and productivity.

sources.title: BLS: Biochemists and Biophysicists
sources.keyEvidence: PhD for independent R&D; some bachelor’s/master’s entry roles. Many PhD holders begin with temporary postdoctoral research.

sources.title: BLS: Hydrologists
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s entry; some employers prefer master’s. Measure water and analyze floods, drought and supply; office plus field work.

sources.title: BLS: Cartographers and Photogrammetrists
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s entry; use geographic data to make maps. Licensing varies by duties, employer and state; certification usually optional.

sources.title: BLS: Financial Examiners
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s including accounting; entry examiners train under seniors. Financial institution soundness and regulatory/consumer compliance.

sources.title: BLS: Financial Analysts
sources.keyEvidence: Financial risk specialists assess credit and market exposures, develop risk controls; bachelor’s typical. Distinct detailed occupation from investment analysts.

sources.title: O*NET: Financial Risk Specialists
sources.keyEvidence: 13-2054.00 distinct from financial and investment analysts.

sources.title: BLS: Purchasing Managers, Buyers, and Purchasing Agents
sources.keyEvidence: Purchasing agents typically bachelor’s, some employers accept high school; training after entry. Purchasing managers need related experience and must stay separate.

sources.title: BLS: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s plus related work experience; analyze pay/benefits and evaluate jobs. BLS related experience category less than five years.

sources.title: BLS: Training and Development Specialists
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s plus work experience; assess employee learning needs, build and deliver training. BLS related experience category less than five years.

sources.title: BLS: Fundraisers
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s typical; nonprofit internship or volunteering preferred by some employers. Research donors, ask for gifts, run and evaluate campaigns.

sources.title: BLS: Technical Writers
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s typical and technical knowledge beneficial. Quick facts identify related experience less than five years and short on-job training.

sources.title: BLS: News Analysts, Reporters, and Journalists
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s typical; student media/internships useful. Interview, research, verify and report news; projected employment decline must remain visible.

sources.title: BLS: Interior Designers
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s typical; plan safe functional interiors. Practice/title law and examination/experience requirements vary by state.

sources.title: BLS: Landscape Architects
sources.keyEvidence: Design outdoor spaces; all states require licensing, usually accredited degree, internship and exam. Supervised preparation is separate from independent practice.

sources.title: BLS: Special Education Teachers
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s and public-school state certification/licensure; adapt lessons, develop IEPs, track individual progress. BLS publishes broader kindergarten/elementary grouping.

sources.title: O*NET: Special Education Teachers, Elementary School
sources.keyEvidence: Current O*NET elementary code is 25-2056.00. Older 25-2052.00 is no longer used by O*NET and splits to kindergarten and elementary.

sources.title: BLS: Probation Officers and Correctional Treatment Specialists
sources.keyEvidence: Bachelor’s typical; government training, possible certification/competency tests and trainee period; legal supervision and rehabilitation responsibilities.

sources.title: BLS: Anthropologists and Archeologists
sources.keyEvidence: Master’s typical, some require PhD. Field training/internships preferred; some bachelor’s graduates start as field/lab technicians or research assistants.

sources.title: BLS: Archivists, Curators, and Museum Workers
sources.keyEvidence: Curators typically master’s; collections research, acquisition and exhibitions. Museum technician bachelor’s route is distinct; internships/volunteering helpful.

sources.title: BLS: Occupational Projections and Worker Characteristics
sources.keyEvidence: Detailed SOC/entry classifications; animal and soil/plant scientists bachelor’s; financial risk bachelor’s no related experience; training and technical writing flag related experience. No wage values imported.

findings.title: Missing scientific routes can flatten existing interests
findings.finding: The catalog already includes crops farmwork, veterinary medicine, food science and environmental science, but lacks soil/plant science, animal science, wildlife biology, microbiology and hydrology. Add explicit scientific inquiry choices before inferring whether plant/animal interest is mainly hands-on care, research or treatment.

findings.title: Helping and teaching are broader than clinical practice and school classrooms
findings.finding: Health education, genetic counseling, sports-injury care, special education and adult workplace learning represent distinct combinations. Use contrasts about the actual recipient, problem and responsibility; broad empathy should trigger invitations across relevant branches without confirming all of them.

findings.title: Business breadth needs objects of decisions, not title prestige
findings.finding: Procurement, financial examination, financial risk, compensation and fundraising have different defining decisions. Ask whether the student wants to choose suppliers, examine compliance, manage uncertainty, analyze rewards or ask for mission support.

findings.title: Writing/design breadth needs mode and purpose contrasts
findings.finding: Factual investigation, technical explanation, fictional/general authorship, indoor spatial design and outdoor design can share broad artistic scores while requiring different interests.

findings.title: Route and experience safeguards must survive catalog expansion
findings.finding: Technical writing, compensation analysis and workplace learning have related-experience flags in BLS. Landscape architecture has a supervised licensing path. Graduate scientific work can begin with lower-responsibility research or postdoctoral stages. A match can be an interest match before the full role is attainable, but the first-paid-stage budget must use the appropriate stage.

findings.title: Do not inflate variety by duplicating subtypes
findings.finding: Use one catalog occupation per detailed SOC when work is materially the same, with optional specialization tags. Preserve O*NET-to-BLS crosswalks where detail differs, such as elementary special education. A new title without a distinct task/interest contrast does not add useful coverage.

questionDesignRecommendations: Start with several independently selectable objects and purposes: people’s health, communities, living organisms, materials, machines, places, information, money, culture and learning. Do not require a single field to be chosen before seeing cross-field occupations.

Invite on partial transferable evidence, then distinguish domain-specific learning interest from current skill, terminology familiarity, training willingness, working conditions and independent practice authority.
Ask two complementary defining activities plus a nearby-role contrast; allow both, neither and need an example. A contrast routes exploration; it is not a forced ranking or an automatic veto.
Offer a concrete short example for unfamiliar work; ask learning interest again after exposure. Keep explicit disinterest separate from unfamiliarity and missing biography evidence.
Treat diverse combinations explicitly: health plus teaching, biology plus counseling, art plus spatial reasoning, justice plus rehabilitation, numbers plus regulation.

Test false positives as well as recall: sports without patient-care interest, loving animals without research/treatment interest, writing without factual verification, liking attractive rooms without spatial/function design, generosity without solicitation interest.
Use versioned, preregistered question/evidence rules and independent biography-only answers before rerunning. Keep old and new offers, domain confirmation and preparation status visible together.

Top eligibility should require a defensible combination of broad interest and defining-work support, not the number of duplicated questions or occupational prestige. Do not require every optional specialty or tool as a universal core gate.

These editorial prompts need readability review, student cognitive interviews, exposure-bias review and outcome validation before claims about accuracy or aptitude; synthetic model replays are regression checks, not validation of real students.

waves.label: First breadth wave
waves.priorityBasis: Distinct missing work domains close to existing fields, with concrete discriminating activities; preparation flags still apply.

waves.label: Second breadth wave
waves.priorityBasis: Graduate, experience-dependent or narrower specialties requiring fuller route budgets and branching before activation.

occupations.title: Health Education Specialists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s degree; some positions require graduate study
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: None in BLS typical entry classification; internships can help
occupations.licensingCertification: Some employers require or prefer professional certification; no universal clinical-practice license inferred
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to find out what health information a community needs and create a workshop or resource that helps people use it?
Would you like to learn to check whether a health education program is helping people and improve it from their feedback?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: teach people ways to protect their health, or provide hands-on clinical treatment to an individual patient?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds nonclinical health-plus-teaching work, preventing every helping or prevention interest from being routed into nursing or diagnosis.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s degree in occupational health/safety or related field; some jobs master’s
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: No universal prior-work requirement; some employers prefer industry experience
occupations.licensingCertification: Employer-dependent certification may require education, experience and exam; distinguish specialist from technician
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to inspect a workplace and find conditions or work habits that could injure people?
Would you like to learn to investigate why an incident happened and recommend changes that make the work safer?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: prevent injuries by changing how a workplace operates, or respond to dangerous situations once an emergency happens?
occupations.coverageAdded: Captures preventive safety investigation rather than emergency response, environmental pollution research, or production optimization.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Genetic Counselors
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Master’s in genetic counseling, normally after bachelor’s; supervised clinical rotations
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: Clinical training is part of preparation; do not invent independent prior employment requirement
occupations.licensingCertification: Most states license; accredited master’s plus exam for certification; employers may require certification even where not mandated
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn how family health history and genetic test results can show a person's chance of an inherited condition?
Would you like to learn to explain genetic risks and testing choices to a worried person while supporting their own decision?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: interpret genetic information with patients and families, or investigate genes through laboratory experiments?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds a specific science-and-counseling bridge; empathy alone or biology alone should invite exploration but cannot confirm this combined role.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Athletic Trainers
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Master’s from an accredited athletic training program
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: Clinical components during preparation; distinguish entry athletic trainer from head trainer
occupations.licensingCertification: Nearly all states require licensure or certification; qualifying exam and continuing education usually apply
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to recognize and evaluate a sports or activity injury and decide what immediate care is needed?
Would you like to learn to guide injury rehabilitation and prevention with an athlete and their health care team?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: treat and prevent activity-related injuries, or coach people mainly to improve fitness and performance?
occupations.coverageAdded: Captures clinical sports-injury interest missing between exercise physiology, emergency response and broader physical therapy; enjoying sports is insufficient.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Microbiologists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s microbiology or related field; some employers prefer master’s/PhD
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification
occupations.licensingCertification: No universal license stated in BLS overview; clinical diagnostic roles require their own regulatory review
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to grow and identify microorganisms to investigate what they do?
Would you like to learn to design a careful laboratory comparison of how bacteria or fungi respond to different conditions?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: study how microscopic organisms behave, or test patient samples mainly to support a clinical diagnosis?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds scientist-level microbial inquiry distinct from assisting researchers, general chemistry and food-product science.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s entry; master’s may be needed for higher-level work; PhD commonly to lead research
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification
occupations.licensingCertification: No general license asserted; permits and field requirements depend on activity
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to observe wildlife and record evidence about how animals behave and use their habitat?
Would you like to learn to compare animal population data and investigate how habitat changes affect survival?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: study wild animal populations and habitats, or diagnose and treat an individual animal's illness?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds animal/ecosystem research without forcing an animal-interested student into veterinary medicine or broad land management.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Soil and Plant Scientists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s typical entry; specialized research may require graduate study
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification
occupations.licensingCertification: Some plant/soil work requires state licensure, supervised experience and exam; certification generally not universal
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to compare soil, water, or growing conditions to find out why crops and other plants thrive or struggle?
Would you like to learn to test a growing method and use the results to improve plant health or crop production?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: investigate why plants grow differently through experiments, or spend most of the day planting and caring for them hands-on?
occupations.coverageAdded: Provides a college research path for growing/plant interests; farmwork interest alone should not imply experimental science, but can justify this invitation.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Animal Scientists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s typical BLS entry; advanced research can require master’s/PhD
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification
occupations.licensingCertification: No universal certificate asserted; distinguish this research occupation from veterinary licensure
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to investigate how feed and living conditions affect farm animals' growth and health?
Would you like to learn to compare evidence about animal nutrition or reproduction and recommend better husbandry methods?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: investigate how groups of farm animals grow and develop, or provide medical treatment to individual animals?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds agricultural animal biology and nutrition research, distinct from veterinary diagnosis and food-product development.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Biochemists and Biophysicists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Doctoral/professional degree is BLS typical classification; some bachelor’s/master’s entry positions exist
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: Independent R&D commonly PhD; temporary postdoctoral stage common after doctorate
occupations.licensingCertification: No clinical-practice license implied by research role
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to investigate how molecules inside living cells make processes such as growth or disease happen?
Would you like to learn to design a laboratory experiment that tests how a substance changes a biological process?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: investigate chemical processes inside living cells, or study materials and reactions mainly outside living systems?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds molecular biological research between chemistry and medical-device engineering; graduate route and first paid research stage need explicit budgeting.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Hydrologists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s hydrology/geology or related field; some employers prefer master’s
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification
occupations.licensingCertification: No universal credential asserted from OOH; local practice requirements must be verified
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to measure streams or groundwater and investigate how water moves through a place?
Would you like to learn to use rainfall and water data to estimate flood risk or future water supply?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: study how water moves and changes, or design and construct the pipes, dams, or drainage systems that control it?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds water-cycle science, distinguishing scientific investigation from pollution generalism and infrastructure design.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Cartographers and Photogrammetrists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s in cartography, geography, geomatics or related field
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification; GIS internships helpful
occupations.licensingCertification: Licensing depends on duties/state/employer; certification usually optional
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to turn location data and aerial images into an accurate map people can use?
Would you like to learn to compare map layers to reveal patterns such as access to services, flooding, or changes in land use?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: analyze and display geographic information, or decide the policies and development plans a community should adopt?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds geographic analysis and mapping at the intersection of data, visual communication and environment without assuming urban-policy interest.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Financial Examiners
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s including accounting coursework
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: Entry examiners train under seniors; long-term on-job training, no prior related occupation in BLS typical classification
occupations.licensingCertification: Professional credentials may support advancement; do not impose CPA as universal entry requirement
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to examine a bank's records to check whether it is financially sound and following lending rules?
Would you like to learn to document a financial compliance problem and explain what needs to change?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: check whether financial institutions follow rules and protect customers, or recommend investments to improve returns?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds regulatory/consumer financial investigation; it is not another investment-advice title or an automatic law match.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Financial Risk Specialists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s typical; some employers prefer master’s
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification
occupations.licensingCertification: Optional professional credentials are distinct from licenses for particular regulated securities activities
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to use data to estimate how much a business could lose if markets change or borrowers cannot repay?
Would you like to learn to compare ways of limiting financial losses and explain the trade-offs to decision makers?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: estimate and limit financial losses, or choose investments mainly for their potential return?
occupations.coverageAdded: A distinct SOC focused on downside exposure and controls, rather than investment selection. Avoid duplicating existing financial-analysis offers under two names.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Purchasing Agents, Except Wholesale, Retail, and Farm Products
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s typical; some employers accept high school preparation
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: Moderate on-job training; managerial purchasing roles require prior related work and are separate
occupations.licensingCertification: Certification may be helpful; do not turn voluntary credentials into a universal legal gate
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to compare suppliers on quality, reliability, and price to decide what an organization should buy?
Would you like to learn to negotiate an order and check that the supplier delivers what was agreed?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: select and negotiate with suppliers for an organization, or persuade customers to buy that organization's products?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds buyer-side commercial decision making, separate from moving goods, selling them or coordinating an entire project.
occupations.implementationNote: BLS groups buyers and purchasing agents as 13-1020 for some wage/entry tables; use exact O*NET 13-1023.00 for non-retail/non-farm purchasing. Do not attach manager wages.

occupations.title: Compensation, Benefits, and Job Analysis Specialists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s plus related work experience
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: BLS less than five years of related experience; requires an earlier paid HR/business stage in planning
occupations.licensingCertification: Professional certification may be useful; no universal practice license asserted
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to compare job responsibilities and pay data to work out fair and competitive compensation?
Would you like to learn to compare employee benefit plans and explain their costs and value to an organization?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: analyze jobs, pay, and benefit systems, or spend most of your time recruiting and interviewing applicants?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds quantitative reward/job evaluation work beyond the catalog's broad recruiting-oriented HR role; relevant as a longer route with experience.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Training and Development Specialists

occupations.experiencePrerequisite: BLS less than five years related work experience; experience may come from teaching, HR or a field being taught

learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to find out what employees need to learn and design a useful practice activity or short course?
Would you like to learn to lead workplace training and improve it after checking whether employees can use the new skill?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: help adults learn skills they use at work, or teach school-age students an academic curriculum?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds adult learning and practical workplace instruction; teaching interests need not imply classroom school teaching.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Fundraisers
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s typical entry
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: No related occupation in BLS typical classification; nonprofit internship/volunteering preferred by some employers
occupations.licensingCertification: No universal fundraiser certificate asserted; organizational solicitation rules require separate review
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to explain a cause to potential donors and ask them to contribute money or other support?
Would you like to learn to plan a fundraising campaign and use its results to improve the next one?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: persuade donors to fund an organization's mission, or provide the organization's direct services to people who need help?

occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: Technical Writers

occupations.licensingCertification: Professional certification is not a universal legal requirement
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn how a technical product or process works so you can write clear instructions for its users?

occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: explain accurately how a real product or process works, or invent characters and stories for readers?
occupations.coverageAdded: Adds explanatory technical communication rather than fictional/general authorship; preserves a writing-plus-science/technology path.
occupations.implementationNote: New editorial questions are draft exploration items, not validated aptitude measures. Interest is separate from preparation and affordability.

occupations.title: News Analysts, Reporters, and Journalists
occupations.typicalEntryEducation: Bachelor’s typical; student media and internships helpful
occupations.experiencePrerequisite: No related work experience in BLS typical entry classification; portfolio/practical reporting experience helps
occupations.licensingCertification: No general journalist practice license inferred; ordinary access/press credentials are not entry degrees
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to interview people and check records to find out what really happened in a newsworthy event?
Would you like to learn to turn verified facts and different viewpoints into a clear report for the public?
occupations.contrastQuestion: Which would you rather learn: independently investigate and report an issue, or communicate a favorable message on behalf of an organization?

occupations.title: Interior Designers

occupations.licensingCertification: Practice and title laws vary by state; some examination routes require degree and experience
learnInterestQuestions: Would you like to learn to plan indoor spaces around how people move, work, and live in them?
